# BloodLens — Decision Brief

**Niche:** AI-powered personal blood test interpretation and longitudinal health tracking
**ICP:** Health-conscious adults aged 30-60 who get regular blood work done, biohackers, patients managing chronic conditions (diabetes, thyroid, cholesterol), and wellness enthusiasts who want to understand and optimize their biomarkers over time but lack medical expertise to interpret results.

## Strategy
The core pain point—fragmented blood test data with no accessible interpretation—is universal and growing as consumers take more ownership of their health. The freemium model lowers the barrier to entry, allowing users to experience the AI interpretation value immediately, which drives organic word-of-mouth (people share health discoveries). The $9 Plus tier captures the regular-testing crowd (2-4x/year testers) who need historical tracking, while the $19 Pro tier targets biohackers and chronic condition patients who test frequently and want predictive insights. HIPAA compliance is table-stakes and a trust moat. The key strategic differentiator is the longitudinal intelligence layer—competitors offer one-time interpretation, but BloodLens becomes more valuable over time as it accumulates data, creating strong retention and switching costs. Lab provider partnerships (Quest, Labcorp) via API integrations reduce upload friction and create a distribution channel. The lifestyle correlation engine transforms BloodLens from a passive record-keeper into an active health optimization tool, justifying recurring subscription revenue. Early focus should be on OCR upload quality and AI interpretation accuracy to build trust, then expand into lab partnerships for seamless data flow.
